transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-11
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (CTO, Orion BioSystems), Graham Holt (Head of Infra), Ana Ruiz (Security Architect), Samir Khan (ML Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen - may be imperfect):
- Purpose: scope a Private POC for Redwood Private/Dedicated with strict EU data residency and egress controls.
- Key asks: VPC peering vs PrivateLink options, proof of no public egress, benchmarks for latency and throughput, timeline for a 3-week POC.
- Next steps: exchange security docs, share network CIDRs, schedule benchmark window.

Topics:
- POC success criteria, throughput/latency targets, benchmark shape
- Networking: VPC peering, PrivateLink, interface endpoints, cross-account peering, Transit Gateway concerns

- Egress constraints: deny internet, route to on-prem SIEM, egress via customer NAT/gateway
- Ops and logs: audit logs, KMS, SSO, SAML, RBAC

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros - I'm Lena, AE on the account, Marcus here is our systems engineer.
[00:14] Marcus Li: Hi folks. I'll be driving the bench plan and network walkthroughs.
[00:22] Priya Desai: Thanks. Priya here, CTO at Orion. We, um, want to make sure we can keep all PHI-ish data in EU regions and block any outbound to public internet.
[00:33] Graham Holt: Graham - we run AWS across eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. Our compliance team is asking for strong guarantees on egress.
[00:41] Ana Ruiz: Ana - security. We need KMS-managed keys, audit logs forwarded to our Splunk, and VPC-level controls.
[00:48] Samir Khan: Samir - ML Eng. We'll be running token-heavy workloads, some long contexts (2k+ tokens). We'll need to size the instance and get latency numbers.
[01:05] Lena Park: Great. So big picture: Redwood can run Private in your VPC or Dedicated in our environment with VPC peering / PrivateLink to restrict network paths. Marcus, can you quick-surface the main tradeoffs?
[01:20] Marcus Li: Yeah. Two common patterns: VPC Peering (cross-account peering) gives direct networking and lower latency but requires route table additions and possibly Transit Gateway if scale is large. PrivateLink (Interface endpoints) is easier for per-service controlled access and avoids route table complexity, but it goes through AWS ENIs and has cross-az considerations; egress is still controlled. For strict no-internet egress we recommend a model where all outbound goes through customer egress NAT or firewall; Redwood will not initiate public calls.
[01:55] Priya Desai: So for the ATO we're looking for proof that traffic never leaves EU, and that logs and model artifacts are stored in region. Can Redwood guarantee that?
[02:08] Marcus Li: We can pin inference nodes to EU regions and our control plane can be configured to operate in region-limited mode. For Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed in your VPC so that metadata doesn't leave region. For Dedicated there are options to pin to EU-only. We'll share architecture notes in the security pack.
[02:28] Ana Ruiz: What about key management? We require customer KMS and no plaintext model weights on disk.
[02:34] Lena Park: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption at rest. Marcus, note to add KMS details to the doc.
[02:44] Marcus Li: Yep, will add: envelope encryption, KMS CMKs, and guidance for HSM if needed.
[02:50] Graham Holt: On networking specifics: our infra uses TGW — we prefer not to add many peering relations. Is Redwood compatible with Transit Gateway?
[02:59] Marcus Li: Yes. We can peer with TGW via an account peering or use PrivateLink endpoints per account in our recommended pattern. The TGW adds some route propagation nuance but it's supported. For scale, TGW is often easier.
[03:12] Priya Desai: Good. Now benchmarks. Samir, can you talk through our expected workload and what success looks like?
[03:20] Samir Khan: Sure. Our primary workload is clinical summarization and structured extraction. Typical context 1k-2k tokens, some up to 5k during note stitching. Expected concurrency during business hours: 20-50 reqs/min across team, peak bursts to 200 concurrent requests over a 10-minute window for backfill. We need p95 latency under 300ms for 512-token completions and ideally under 1s for 2k token scenarios. Cost target is an internal target: keep inference spend under $0.50 per 1k tokens (ballpark).
[03:55] Marcus Li: For sizing: we'll propose a baseline 4-GPU pool for the POC (NVIDIA A100-style equivalency) and run three bench types: small (512 tokens), medium (2k tokens), long (5k tokens). We'll measure throughput (tokens/s), p50/p95 latency, and GPU utilization. Also run KV cache warm/cold tests to see impact.
[04:20] Priya Desai: Timeline — we're hoping to move quickly. Can we do a 3-week POC? Week 1: network and infra setup, week 2: bench runs and integration, week 3: validation and handover.
[04:33] Lena Park: That sounds doable. We'll need network bits and security approvals quickly to hit that.
[04:40] Graham Holt: On egress — we have a strict rule: no outbound to internet except to our Splunk and a few vendor endpoints which we vet. How does Redwood ship logs?
[04:51] Marcus Li: Logs can be forwarded to your syslog/Splunk via a pull model or push over a private peering. We also support forwarding audit logs to an S3 bucket in your account (EU region) — that bucket can be locked down.
[05:05] Ana Ruiz: S3-based logs are fine. We must ensure retention policies and encryption. Also need proof of access controls and RBAC.
[05:14] Lena Park: We'll include an RBAC doc and sample Terraform snippets for bucket policies.
[05:20] Priya Desai: Regarding data residency, if we have some UK data that needs UK-only residency, does Redwood support region-level splits?
[05:29] Marcus Li: Yes, you can route requests to region-specific endpoints. For Private deployments you can deploy stacks per region. For Dedicated we can pin model pools to region. There's some operational complexity but it's standard.
[05:40] Samir Khan: One more on benchmarks: we also want to test model-fallback behavior. If capacity is constrained, can Redwood do auto-fallback to a smaller quantized model without changing the API?
[05:50] Marcus Li: Yes — routing policies can fallback to quantized variants, or lower-cost families. We'll include a canary/fallback test in the bench plan. Note: quantization affects output quality; we'll include quality regression checks with a prompt set.
[06:05] Priya Desai: Ok. On the legal side, our procurement team will want a data processing addendum and clarity on subprocessor list.
[06:14] Lena Park: We'll loop in legal; I'll send the DPA and a redacted subprocessor list.
[06:19] Graham Holt: For network setup, do you need us to open any specific ports? We prefer not to open anything except 443 outbound to the PrivateLink endpoints.
[06:29] Marcus Li: For PrivateLink, 443 to the endpoint ENIs is typical. For VPC peering, it's all internal and no public ports needed. We'll provide a minimal security group/TLS fingerprint guide.
[06:42] Ana Ruiz: Does Redwood require any outbound DNS resolution to public resolvers? We force all DNS to our internal resolvers.
[06:49] Marcus Li: No public DNS required — we can support private DNS via Route53 private hosted zones, or you can point to your resolver. We'll document the options.
[06:58] Samir Khan: Regarding metrics we want to collect during benches: GPU utilization, memory, tokens/sec, p50/p95, error rates, tail latencies for KV cache misses. Also cold-start behavior for long contexts.
[07:12] Marcus Li: We'll add those metrics and export them to Prometheus push gateway or CloudWatch metrics forwarded to your account.
[07:20] Lena Park: Let's capture POC success criteria explicitly now so we have alignment. Priya, do you want to propose a short list?
[07:27] Priya Desai: Sure. Success criteria: 1) All traffic and logs remain in EU region; 2) p95 latency <= 300ms for 512-token completion, <= 1.2s for 2k token; 3) throughput: sustain 200 concurrent with degradation graceful; 4) audit logs visible in our Splunk within 60s; 5) no public internet egress for inference traffic.
[07:51] Marcus Li: We'll map the bench pass/fail to each criterion; for the 200 concurrent target we'll show modeled cost and possible autoscale rules.
[07:59] Graham Holt: Cost — you mentioned Dedicated vs Private. Can you outline the high-level cost tradeoffs?
[08:06] Lena Park: Briefly: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's account—predictable throughput and lower management overhead; Private is deployed into your VPC and gives you more control (and can be pricier for single-customer stacks due to operational footprint). We'll send a cost comparison for the dev/prod variants.
[08:20] Priya Desai: For procurement we need pricing ballparks: dev POC pool, and prod steady-state.
[08:26] Lena Park: We'll include a ballistic estimate in the follow-up.
[08:29] Samir Khan: Any known gotchas for long-context (5k) runs — memory or KV cache tuning?
[08:35] Marcus Li: Long contexts hit KV cache and memory. We'll recommend quantization profile for long-contexts to save memory and propose a caching layer; we'll include concrete kernel/compilation notes in the bench doc.
[08:48] Priya Desai: One of our constraints: internal policy forbids cross-account access to S3 except via VPC endpoints. Can logs be pushed to our vpc endpoint-only S3?
[08:58] Marcus Li: Yes, we can write logs to an S3 bucket in your account via a role that assumes into your account over the private link. We'll document the IAM role and minimal permissions.
[09:11] Ana Ruiz: Also need SIEM integration — Splunk HEC token rotation and IP allowlisting.
[09:18] Marcus Li: We'll support pushing via a secure webhook over the peering; token rotation is supported. We'll include sample configs.
[09:25] Lena Park: Excellent. Let's talk about the bench window scheduling. We propose week of 2025-08-18. Is that workable?
[09:33] Priya Desai: Yes, but we need Graham to confirm network windows.
[09:37] Graham Holt: I'll confirm but tentatively yes. I need the exact time and expected traffic so we can coordinate TGW route propagation.
[09:46] Marcus Li: We'll provide a bench plan with time-of-day, expected IPs, and load shape. Also will include a fall-back rollback plan.
[09:54] Samir Khan: On the evals: we want to run a quality regression harness — same prompt set across model variants and quantized vs float. We need transcripts compared and a small human review sample.
[10:05] Marcus Li: We'll include that. We'll also export generation deltas and token-level diffs.
[10:12] Priya Desai: Any examples of other customers who ran EU-only POCs?
[10:18] Lena Park: We have a couple — we can redacted-share short case notes. Marcus will include an anonymized reference.
[10:26] Graham Holt: Security question: incident response — in case of suspected exfil, what are the detection and containment steps?
[10:33] Marcus Li: We provide audit trails with user-level actions, request traces, and the ability to revoke keys and rotate. For Private we can isolate the control plane and shut off connectivity quickly. We'll include an IR playbook excerpt.
[10:47] Ana Ruiz: Good. We will also need SLA and MTTR numbers for incidents that impact inference.
[10:53] Lena Park: We'll share SLA tiers and our typical MTTR targets with examples.
[11:00] Priya Desai: Okay last bit — can Redwood run in our account (on-prem-ish) behind our firewall? We have a hybrid environment that is partly air-gapped for certain data.
[11:09] Marcus Li: There is an on-prem package for air-gapped needs; for the POC that tends to add time. If you have strict air-gapped needs we should talk separately — but we support it.
[11:20] Lena Park: Great. Let's recap the action items and next steps.
[11:27] Lena Park: Action items: 1) Redwood to send security pack, DPA, bench plan; 2) Customer to share VPC CIDRs, TGW diagram, and residency list; 3) Schedule bench window week of 8/18; 4) Legal exchange DPA.
[11:44] Priya Desai: That matches our notes. Thanks everyone.
[11:48] Graham Holt: Thanks.
[11:50] Ana Ruiz: Thanks, bye.
[11:51] Samir Khan: Bye.
